answers.answer: They cannot win at the next Wake: the Exile victory check happens before an Exile holding Oathkeeper flips it to Usurper. They can first win at the start of their following turn's Wake, if they still hold the title. They can also win as Usurper at the end of round 8 if still Usurper then. Losing the title prevents the Usurper win; if they regain it, it resets to Oathkeeper and the sequence starts again.
answers.evidence: Usurper victory: ‘next Wake check (not yet Usurper), then flip to Usurper, then win at the following Wake or at the end of round 8’; ‘Losing title prevents this win; retaking resets it to Oathkeeper.’

answers.answer: Supremacy pairs with Conquest; People with Rebellion; Protection with Sanctuary; Devotion with Faith. For a Visionary win, an Exile must reveal the true Vision, meet its goal at Wake, and at least 3 Visions must have been drawn from the world deck by all players combined. Ties for ‘most’ do not count for Conquest or Sanctuary: the Exile must have strictly more than every other player.
answers.evidence: ‘Oathkeeper and four Oaths’ table gives the pairs; ‘at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck by all players combined’; ‘most means strictly more than every other player, no ties.’

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. A Citizen meeting its Successor goal wins alone instead of the Chancellor. An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.
answers.evidence: Stable regime: ‘at ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7, roll end die only if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper’; results are ‘6 / 5–6 / 3–6.’

answers.answer: Round 8 ends automatically. Check in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins, with a qualified Citizen Successor winning alone instead of Chancellor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions prioritized Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, with qualified Successor replacing Chancellor. Thus Empire Oathkeeper takes priority over Usurper and Vision, and a Citizen cannot win by Vision or Usurper.
answers.evidence: War exhaustion lists the four priority checks in this order and says Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.

answers.answer: Successor goals: Supremacy—hold more relics and banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen; People—hold Darkest Secret; Protection—hold People's Favor; Devotion—hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win through a revealed true Vision or by becoming Usurper.
answers.evidence: Oath table column ‘Citizen Successor goal’; victory text: ‘Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.’

answers.answer: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, either put 1 favor from your board onto it or return 1 favor from it to a least-full suit bank (choose among tied least-full banks). Never remove its last favor: if it has one, add one if able; if you have none, do nothing. If it is already Mob-side, perform the choice twice. After the choice(s), flip it to Mob if it has at least 6 favor. Becoming Mob at this final threshold check does not cause a second payment that Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake order says Mob-side repeats the choice, last favor is never removed, then ‘if it has 6+ favor, flip to Mob’; the flip does not retroactively repeat that Wake.

answers.answer: Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; (2) return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; (3) refresh Supply—Exile/Chancellor by warbands left in personal bank, while Citizen goes to the exact Chancellor marker space, including the leftmost space; (4) save each remaining unspent Supply by moving the marker one extra space left per point, capped at the leftmost space (7 Supply); (5) optionally use Rest powers, each once in an order you choose. Chancellor refresh is 6/5/4/3 for personal-bank bands 18+/11–17/4–10/0–3; Exile is 6/5/4 for 9+/4–8/0–3.
answers.evidence: Rest mandatory order enumerates these five steps and the Chancellor/Exile thresholds; Citizen uses the ‘exact Chancellor marker space.’

answers.answer: Search costs 2 Supply from your pawn's region discard pile, or from the world deck costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces the world-deck cost with 2, subject to other applicable modifiers. Choose one source, not both. Draw 3 (fewer only if the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops the draw, or a modifier reduces the draw); you cannot voluntarily stop early. From the world deck draw one at a time; on drawing a Vision announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately, and advance Visions Drawn. A Vision from a discard pile does not stop the draw or advance that track. If a source empties, take what remains; no reshuffle is implied.
answers.evidence: Search section specifies sources and costs, mandatory draw amount, world-deck stop/track rule, and that discard-pile Visions do not stop or advance.

answers.answer: Discard facedown atop the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle; order multiple discards as you choose. For hand/adviser cards, choose the destination based on your pawn's region: Cradle pawn to Provinces pile, Provinces pawn to Hinterland, Hinterland pawn to Cradle. Never use the same-region pile. When discarding a card from a site in another region, use the cycle based on that card's region, not your pawn's. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching bank; secrets on it go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: ‘Discard destinations’ gives the region cycle, pawn-region rule, remote-site exception, and resource handling.

answers.answer: You may have up to 3 advisers total, counting faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser if legally possible and respect locks; if the incoming card changes the limit, check the new limit before playing it (use the lowest of multiple limits). A facedown adviser can later be played faceup to a legal destination or discarded as a minor action; it may also be peeked at. A faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will, only when another rule allows/requires it. Any card, including a site-only card or Vision, may be held facedown; facedown advisers have no suit, banner restriction or power. An Exile plays/reveals a true Vision faceup in the separate Revealed Vision slot, replacing and discarding the previously revealed Vision; it does not occupy an adviser slot. Chancellor/Citizens can hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.
answers.evidence: Search adviser options state the 3-card limit and later options; true Vision rule specifies Exile-only separate slot and replacement; Minor actions detail later play.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply. At your pawn's site, choose an empty denizen or intact edifice (no favor/secrets already; relics and ruins are ineligible), place 1 favor on it, and gain 2 warbands from your personal bank to your board (Citizens gain purple). You need not rule the site. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses the same eligible empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site. Option A: place 1 secret on it and gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank. Option B: place 2 favor on it and gain 1 secret from the shared bank per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers never match; with no matching faceup advisers option B yields zero secrets, but the two-favor cost is still paid. Favor/warbands are limited by available supply; secrets are unlimited.
answers.evidence: Muster and Trade sections specify Supply costs, eligibility, placement and gains; Trade says no matching advisers gives zero secrets and costs remain payable.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target's cost. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay its printed site Recover cost (3 favor to indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in your personal bank. A banner of either type can be recovered from anywhere, including a player or shared bank, for any amount of its resource strictly greater than its current amount. For People's Favor, place the paid favor on the banner and distribute the old favor one at a time among suit banks, starting at a chosen bank and moving away from the world deck through successive banks, wrapping as needed; do not return old favor to its former holder. Flip it to normal side if Mob. For Darkest Secret, put the paid secrets on it; the new holder takes 1 old secret and the previous holder gets the rest. If recovering it from yourself, all old secrets return to you; if from the shared bank, the remainder stays there. Recovering a banner does not incur the seizure penalty.
answers.evidence: Recover section states the relic target/cost and separate banner outbids and dispositions of old resources.

answers.answer: Another player's Darkest Secret is recoverable only if at their pawn's site there is at least one suited card whose suit matches none of that player's faceup advisers. One such mismatching card suffices even if other cards match. If they have no faceup advisers but there is a suited card at the site, it is recoverable. An empty site protects the banner, as does a ruin-only site, since neither contains a suited card. The protection applies only when recovering from another player; recovering from yourself or the shared bank ignores it.
answers.evidence: Corrected Darkest Secret protection says at least one suited unmatched card; no faceup advisers with a suited site card is recoverable; empty and ruin-only sites protect it.

answers.answer: Choose any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there as defender. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, it must be targeted. You may also target any of that defender's sites anywhere on the map, one defense die per site. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may additionally target any of their relics (their printed defense dice), banners (dice equal to resources on the banner), or their pawn and favor together (2 dice). A relic target at your site satisfies the local-target requirement.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2 specify defender eligibility, local target requirement, remote sites, and co-located pawn/relic/banner targets.

answers.answer: Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in their board force, then modifiers apply. Defense dice are rolled; each double-symbol doubles shields (multipliers stack), then add defending warbands at targeted sites and, if the defender's pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site, the defender's board force; double-symbols multiply shields only. Bandits add 1 defense per targeted bandit site. On attack, each skull immediately kills one of the attacker's force warbands. Count full swords and add 1 for each pair of hollow swords (a leftover single adds zero). The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never extra. Attacker wins only when attack strictly exceeds defense; a tie or lower is defender victory.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2, 4, and 5 specify dice pools, defense additions, skulls, swords, exact sacrifice, and strict-win threshold.

answers.answer: After an attacker victory, first the defender kills half the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board; resolve defeated battle-plan effects. Then the attacker may place any number—including zero—of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero garrisons leaves a site to bandits unless another power applies. The attacker takes all targeted relics and banners. A seized banner (by any means except Recover) loses 2 resources down to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If the pawn and favor were targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site without Supply and may independently burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Observe travel restrictions; if Shrouded Wood's enemy ruler chooses the travel destination, that overrides the attacker's choice. Then resolve the attacker's victorious battle-plan effects and discard plans marked ‘At end, discard.’
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–8 give defeat-before-target sequence, zero placement, banner penalty, forced travel/favor options, Shrouded Wood override, and plan timing.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker site or any targeted site. Defense modifiers from the defender and Allies are activated; they share side-wide powers and title defense bonus, but ‘your site’ and ‘your board’ still refer to each player's own. Allied board warbands add defense only when their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. Allies can use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not other players' advisers; a shared plan can be used once total per Campaign by one paid-for user. The declared defender controls order/timing/priority in disagreements. Chancellor chooses Imperial defending casualties; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while Citizens' surviving board warbands remain on those boards. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make every Citizen non-Imperial: a Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign, and when Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that defender is non-Imperial for it.
answers.evidence: Imperial defense section lists automatic Chancellor ally, permitted Citizen allies, shared powers/plans, casualties and the limited non-Imperial status rule; Campaign step 1 specifies the two cases.

answers.answer: Base Travel Supply costs by origin→destination region are: Cradle→Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; Provinces→Cradle 2, Provinces 2, Hinterland 2; Hinterland→Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Travel is to any different site, not just an adjacent slot. Reveal a facedown destination and stock its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank and its printed number of facedown relics from the relic deck. Apply fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. A final Free Travel override (a power saying ‘spend no Supply’) makes payment zero even if another power increases cost, including for banishment. Site entry restrictions still apply unless specifically ignored. Site modifiers include Coast-to-Coast cost 1 and ignores Narrow Pass; Charming Valley increases cost by 1; Shrouded Wood travel from it costs 2 and ignores Narrow Pass and Hidden Place; Buried Giant may flip one of your board secrets facedown for no Supply and to ignore Narrow Pass; a destination/route restriction such as Narrow Pass or Hidden Place still applies unless a power overrides it.
answers.evidence: Travel table and paragraph give all region costs, reveal/stocks, and ordering; Site powers detail Coasts, Charming Valley, Shrouded Wood, Buried Giant, Narrow Pass and Hidden Place.

answers.answer: During play, the Grand Scepter holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, but not on the turn they took the Scepter. The offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; the parties may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners and non-Reliquary relics, and the recipient may be allowed to peek at Reliquary relics. The recipient accepts by flipping to Citizen and replacing all their own board/map warbands with purple (if purple is short, they choose which to remove and replace), discarding their revealed Vision, flipping their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, ending their Act if it is their turn, and refreshing to full leftmost Supply. They exchange the promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. The Scepter holder may also exile another Citizen under the specified favor payment; a Citizen without Scepter may self-exile by paying the holder favor equal to own board warbands plus all their secrets on board and denizen/relic/edifice cards. In the normal offer, the exact relic gift is required, with optional additional binding exchange; don't infer other compulsory transfers. Forced Citizenship powers use the status-conversion steps without a negotiated offer, relic gift or invented exchange; only actual Reliquary removal uncovers its modifier.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile section specifies offer authority/timing, required gift, optional negotiated exchange, acceptance steps, exile options, and forced-Citizenship exception.

answers.answer: The winner vows the next Oath: a Vision-only victory selects the matching Oath; any other or multiple victory methods allow any Oath except the current one. Save the goal. Chronicle Citizenship is a separate free offer by an Exile winner: no Scepter or relic/resource payment is needed. If the winner is an Exile, first flip all Citizen boards, including boxed ones, to Exile; then the winner may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting Exile flips to Citizen and replaces every garrison at every site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband per site, regardless of old garrison size; winner cannot offer themself this Chronicle Citizenship. To rebuild the world deck, shuffle denizens remaining in play, place 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 cards) in the top stack, 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions (18 cards) in the next stack, and the remaining denizens below. It is not 14 cards because the Chronicle aid's printed ‘12 denizens + 2’ is erroneous; the stated correct top stack is 10 plus 2.
answers.evidence: Chronicle steps 1–2 give Oath and free Citizenship turnover; step 9 states the 10+2 and 15+3 stacks and explicitly corrects the aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ error.
